issues.description: The problem statement (UML) defines numberOfLecturers as an int, but the solution implementation declares the numberOfLecturers attribute as a byte. This mismatch can confuse students about the intended type and lead to inconsistent constructor/setter signatures or unexpected implicit conversions.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the attribute type with the UML/problem statement by changing the solution's numberOfLecturers field to int (and update any related getters/setters/uses). Alternatively, if byte is intentional, update the problem statement/UML to specify byte so students are not misled.

issues.description: The UML and problem description imply the constructor should take numberOfLecturers as an int (following the attribute types), but the solution's constructor declares the corresponding parameter as a byte. This creates a signature mismatch relative to the specification and may confuse students implementing the constructor in the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the solution constructor to accept an int for numberOfLecturers to match the UML and problem description (and adjust the field type accordingly). If the intention is to use byte, update the problem statement/UML to reflect a byte parameter.
